/hold

This looks like it could work to me. Only concern I'm thinking about is the 14 run lookback.

Today we look for 7 days and then 14 days. If you have more runs than 14, great, we will consider those. Looking for 14 runs means that yes, we get the most recent results so will drop older failures, but I think in today's case, if you had 15 runs and only the most recent was a failure, you'd pass and be allowed to promote, where with this the recent failure would block you until it timed out.

Also, does that 14 run lookback get time bounded? If you have fewer than 14 runs in the last two weeks it's not looking further than two weeks back right?

> This looks like it could work to me. Only concern I'm thinking about is the 14 run lookback.
> 
> Today we look for 7 days and then 14 days. If you have more runs than 14, great, we will consider those. Looking for 14 runs means that yes, we get the most recent results so will drop older failures, but I think in today's case, if you had 15 runs and only the most recent was a failure, you'd pass and be allowed to promote, where with this the recent failure would block you until it timed out.

I defaulted to a 14 run lookback because that is what we generally look for, but if we want to consider a wider range to prevent a fluke causing promotion verification failure we can increase it to whatever we deem reasonable. Maybe 25 most recent runs over the last 2 weeks is sufficient?

> Also, does that 14 run lookback get time bounded? If you have fewer than 14 runs in the last two weeks it's not looking further than two weeks back right?

Yes, it is time bound to look no further than 2 weeks back.

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for all review comments with AI agents</summary>

```
Verify each finding against current code. Fix only still-valid issues, skip the
rest with a brief reason, keep changes minimal, and validate.

Inline comments:
In `@tools/codegen/cmd/featuregate-test-analyzer.go`:
- Around line 1092-1104: The hardcoded stub in getJobsForFeatureGateFromSippy is
bypassing the real Sippy lookup and ignoring the release, featureGate, and
variant inputs. Remove the temporary out slice and early return so the function
proceeds to the actual query logic, and keep the existing
getJobsForFeatureGateFromSippy path using the provided parameters to fetch the
correct jobs.
- Around line 1046-1078: The triage handling in verifyJobPassRate is too coarse
and is using all job runs in the pass-rate calculation, which causes triaged
failures to suppress unrelated variants and still count against the denominator.
Update the flow around getTriagedTestFailuresFromSippy and verifyJobPassRate so
triage is keyed by the full variant identity returned by Sippy, not just test
name, and filter out triaged failures before setting
TestResults.TotalRuns/SuccessfulRuns/FailedRuns. Make sure the loop over jobRuns
only increments failures for non-triaged failing runs and that pass-rate math
reflects the filtered set consistently in both affected call sites.
- Around line 1051-1052: The triage lookup result from
getTriagedTestFailuresFromSippy in featuregate-test-analyzer.go is using the
returned err without handling it, which can make failures look untriaged. Update
the logic around triagedTestFailures, err to check and handle the error
immediately: propagate it or stop processing rather than continuing with an
empty triaged set. Keep the fix localized to the code path that consumes
getTriagedTestFailuresFromSippy so the triage counting logic only runs when the
lookup succeeds.
- Around line 999-1008: The defaultTransport setup in featuregate-test-analyzer
should not disable TLS verification for Sippy requests. Remove the
InsecureSkipVerify setting from the tls.Config used by defaultTransport, and
rely on normal certificate validation so the HTTP client still enforces HTTPS
trust checks while preserving the existing transport configuration.
- Around line 993-1016: `verifyInstallFeatureGatePromotion` and the Sippy helper
chain are not propagating cancellation, so requests can outlive `Run(ctx)`.
Update `verifyInstallFeatureGatePromotion` to pass `ctx` into
`getJobsForFeatureGateFromSippy`, then thread it through `getJobRunsFromSippy`
and `getTriagedTestFailuresFromSippy`, and use it when building the HTTP
requests instead of calling `client.Get(...)` directly. Keep the existing
symbols in place, only add context plumbing so request lifetimes follow the
caller’s deadline/cancelation.
```
